fullText:
Disney used a streaming signup to try to keep a widower’s wrongful-death claim out of court.

After his wife died following dinner at Raglan Road in Disney Springs, Jeffrey Piccolo sued. Disney invoked his Disney+ free-trial agreement and park-ticket terms to demand individual arbitration—a private decision-maker instead of court—and argued that the arbitrator should decide whether those terms applied. This concerned courtroom access, not immunity from liability.

The receipt: Case 2024-CA-001616-O, Disney’s May 31, 2024 motion, citing Subscriber Agreement p. 1 and Terms of Use §7: “any dispute between You and Us, Except for Small Claims, is subject to a class action waiver and must be resolved by individual binding arbitration.” Disney abandoned arbitration in August 2024; Piccolo voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit on February 27, 2026. The later dismissal was not an arbitration victory or court approval of Disney’s argument.

Save the signup screen and linked terms. Check which disputes and companies the arbitration clause covers. If your contract offers an opt-out, follow its exact deadline and instructions; keep proof you sent it. NCLC says such windows are often 30 to 60 days—not a verified Disney deadline.
